goal: The worker's active run-log retention reduces the run-logs directory to at or under a configured bound, deleting the oldest run JSONL files while the most-recent runs survive.

graders.run: uv run pytest -k "module_purity or sdk_optional or import_without"
graders.name: purity-holdout

relevant: packages/flywheel-worktree/src/flywheel_worktree/worker.py -- the comment at lines 1013-1016 explicitly leaves .flywheel/logs/runs/ operator-owned and never rotated; this task replaces that disclaimer with an active default-on retention behavior the worker runs

packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/telemetry_file.py -- FileTelemetrySink writes .flywheel/logs/runs/<run_id>.jsonl (runs_dir/path_for); the retention reads this directory, but the reclaim/cap logic must NOT go into flywheel_core.task/lifecycle
constraints: Reclaim the OLDEST run files (by mtime/count) and preserve the most-recent N -- deleting the newest/in-progress run is a defect; a no-op that leaves growth unbounded is the leak this task removes.
The directory is held at or under a CONFIGURED bound (count and/or total size), default-on; magnitude is not load-bearing.
The reclaim logic lives in the telemetry/loaders/worker layer (NOT flywheel_core.task/lifecycle); import flywheel_core must still work without the SDK extra.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not place file/disk/json reclaim logic in flywheel_core.task or flywheel_core.lifecycle (breaks purity -- the purity-holdout grader pins this).
Do not modify or weaken existing telemetry-sink or purity tests; do not weaken assertions.
Do not change the supervisor log bound (separate task).
edge_cases: Distinct mtimes -- the surviving set must be exactly the most-recent N (the test pins WHICH files survive, not just a count).
Fewer files than the bound -- nothing is reclaimed.
An in-progress/newest run must never be the one deleted.
